name: Douglas Hyde Gallery
funding: FY2025 income €695k: Arts Council €378k, Trinity College Dublin €141k, sponsorship €19k, patrons €12k, plus €121k other income mostly from Ireland at Venice 2026 partners.
watch: Director's Circle includes Kerlin Gallery and mother's tankstation. The accounts do not name the Venice 2026 partners. No flagged funder or protest found.
records_note: No annual report; posts 2025 audited accounts, lists a ten-member board, and names its Arts Council and Trinity College support plus tiered patrons, undated.

name: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art
funding: Private centre founded by Leoš Válka (property).
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2014 to 2016, with accounting statements in the 2015 one, and shows undated partner logos; no board list.

name: Dundee Contemporary Arts
funding: £2.8M income (FY2025). Creative Scotland and Dundee; University of Dundee partner; supporters include Paul Hamlyn, Art Fund, Garfield Weston, Henry Moore Foundation, Screen Scotland, Whyte & Mackay.
watch: Baillie Gifford is not among its supporters. No protest, boycott or flagged funder found.
records_note: Annual report and accounts for 2024-25 are on its site and OSCR; funders appear as footer logos only; trustees are listed.

name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
funding: Dunedin City Council gallery. Gallery Partners are Creative New Zealand, Quartz Reef and Craigs Investment Partners; the DPAG Society buys works.
watch: Founding partners in 1996 included Mobil Oil New Zealand and the Lotteries Board; neither is a current funder.
records_note: A council unit with no reports or accounts of its own. Its supporters page names gallery partners and benefactors; staff are listed, no board.

name: Eastside Projects
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, Birmingham City University (partner since 2008), and trusts including the Paul Hamlyn, Esmée Fairbairn, Jerwood and Henry Moore foundations.
watch: Its undated supporters list credits Genting Casino alongside past funders such as the Future Jobs Fund. No current gambling funding found.
records_note: No annual reports; Companies House holds micro-company accounts to March 2025; the supporters list is cumulative and undated, and no board is listed.

name: Echigo-Tsumari Art Triennale
funding: 2024: JPY 360M committee budget and 545,931 visits. Paid for by Tokamachi/Tsunan, Agency for Cultural Affairs/JAC, tickets and furusato-nozei gifts.
watch: TEPCO Niigata (Fukushima operator) is a corporate supporter, giving staff and a venue in kind. The report does not name its 30 corporate donors (JPY 21M).
records_note: The committee posts summary reports for 2018, 2022 and 2024 with accounts and officers, and the support page names sponsors without a date.

name: EKKM (Contemporary Art Museum of Estonia)
funding: Cultural Endowment of Estonia (Eesti Kultuurkapital), Tallinn Culture and Sports Department; artist-governed cooperative non-profit.

name: El Museo del Barrio
funding: Ford Foundation and MacKenzie Scott lead (2024 list); NYC/NYSCA public money, banks (BofA, Morgan Stanley), Maestro Dobel tequila.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies is on the roster (plus Bloomberg Connects), per an Aug 2024 copy. Activists protested the museum's mission at its 50th, June 2019.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, a 2024 supporters list names donors by giving tier, and trustees are listed.

name: EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art
funding: City of Espoo, plus the Saastamoinen Foundation collection.
records_note: Posts activity reports for 2006 to 2024 with key financial figures, names its two main corporate partners and lists its board; no full statements.

name: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Greek state €40M by 2020, plus €3M from the Stavros Niarchos Foundation (shipping).
watch: 2019 governance dispute over the director, not a funding issue.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the footer shows undated logos for the Culture Ministry, SNF and Samsung, and the site names a nine-member administrative board.

name: Enjoy Contemporary Art Space
funding: Creative New Zealand, Wellington City Council; registered non-profit charitable trust.
watch: Wellington's longest-running independent artist-run space on Left Bank; free public exhibitions and critical writing.

name: Erarta Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Private: founded 2010 by Marina Varvarina (widow of Orimi tea-and-coffee group owner Dmitry Varvarin); the museum states it has never taken state support, grants or sponsors.
watch: 12,000 sq m, c. 40 exhibitions a year; c. US$30–35m invested in the building. No sanctions match for Varvarina on OpenSanctions.
records_note: The museum states it takes no state money, grants or sponsors; its site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.
